subject: Model runs even without providing values in data block

messages.author: f8a4136bfeaed71c
messages.subject: Model runs even without providing values in data block
parts:
Hi all,

I have seen a problem that the model still runs even without providing values for the data block. The codes is as follows:

data {
int<lower=1> N; // Sample size
int<lower=2> Ncate;

int<lower=0> NY1;
int<lower=0> NY2;
int<lower=0> NY3;

int indY[N];
}

parameters {
ordered[Ncate-1] cutpoint;

vector<                               upper=cutpoint[1]>[NY1] Z1;
vector<lower=cutpoint[1], upper=cutpoint[2]>[NY2] Z2;
vector<lower=cutpoint[2]>[NY3] Z3;

}

transformed parameters {
real Z[N];

for (i in 1: NY1){
Z[indY[i]] = Z1[i];
}

for (i in 1: NY2){
Z[indY[NY1 + i]] = Z2[i];
}

for (i in 1: NY3){
Z[indY[NY1 + NY2 + i]] = Z3[i];
}
}

model {
Z ~ normal(0, 1);
}

In the first run, I run:

data1 = list(N=ssize, Ncate=3, NY1=NY1, NY2=NY2, NY3=NY3,
               indY=indY)

model1 = stan(file="model1.stan", data = data1,
              iter=2000, chains = 3, pars = 'cutpoint')

And in the second, I run:
data2 = list(N=ssize, Ncate=3, NY1=NY1, NY2=NY2, NY3=NY3)

model2 = stan(file="model2.stan", data = data2,
              iter=2000, chains = 3, pars = 'cutpoint')

Here model2.stan is a copy of model1.stan. The important difference here is data1 contains indY while data2 does not. However, R still runs and still give output (the same as model1) for model2. That is strange to me because in model2, I do not specify indY. And in that case, I think Stan should report error of unknown variable (indY)

Do you know why is that?

Thank you,
Tran.
